title: Strict-transform flatness comparison for a generically free exact sequence
statement: Let $S$ be an affine scheme and $f:X\to S$ an affine smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] with geometrically integral fibres, meaning integral after every residue-field extension. Let $U\subset S$ be a quasi-compact open and let $\mathcal F$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. Suppose $r\geq0$, $\alpha:\mathcal O_X^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal F$, and an open $W\subset X$ are given, $W\to S$ is surjective, and $\alpha|_W$ is an isomorphism. Put $\mathcal H=\operatorname{coker}\alpha$ and assume $0\to\mathcal O_X^{\oplus r}\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal F\to\mathcal H\to0$ remains exact after pullback along every morphism $T\to S$. For every $U$-admissible blowup $b:S^b\to S$, put $X^b=X\times_SS^b$ and $W^b=W\times_SS^b$. There is an induced short exact sequence of module strict transforms $0\to\mathcal O_{X^b}^{\oplus r}\xrightarrow{\alpha^b}\mathcal F^b\to\mathcal H^b\to0$, compatible with the quotient maps from ordinary pullbacks; in particular the strict transform of $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus r}$ is its ordinary pullback. The open $W^b$ surjects onto $S^b$ and $\alpha^b|_{W^b}$ is an isomorphism. For every $y\in X^b$ with image $t\in S^b$, the stalk $\mathcal F^b_y$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S^b,t}$ if and only if $\mathcal H^b_y$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S^b,t}$. Thus $\mathcal H^b$ is flat over $S^b$ if and only if $\mathcal F^b$ is flat over $S^b$. Fibre products and module pullback are as in [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-module-pullback]. Schemes and quasi-compactness conventions are as in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], quasi-coherence and finite type as in [pqf-def-coherent], finite presentation of module sheaves as in [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], and relative flatness as in [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Admissible blowups retain their finite-type centre ideals [def-nagata-admissible-blowup], and all module strict transforms use those specified ideals [def-trf-module-strict-transform].

proof.text: The cokernel $\mathcal H$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-closure]. It is finite type: compose each local finite free surjection onto $\mathcal F$ with $\mathcal F\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal H$. By [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion], $f$ is flat. Thus $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus r}$ is flat over $S$: its stalk is a finite direct sum of flat base modules, and tensoring it with an injection is the direct sum of the corresponding injections. Apply [lem-trf-module-admissible-blowup-calculus](2) to this free module and the specified blowup centre. Its strict-transform quotient map is an isomorphism, identifying $(\mathcal O_X^{\oplus r})^b$ with $p^*(\mathcal O_X^{\oplus r})=\mathcal O_{X^b}^{\oplus r}$, where $p:X^b\to X$. The last equality sends $c\otimes(a_i)$ to $(ca_i)$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. The same calculus makes $\mathcal F^b$ and $\mathcal H^b$ quasi-coherent of finite type.

source.place: Tag 0815, theorem-flatten-module, paragraph 3; divisors.tex Tag 080F, lemma-strict-transform-flat, and Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-strict-transform-universal-exact] to the assumed universally exact sequence and to the finite-type ideal supplied by [def-nagata-admissible-blowup]. Substitute the free-term identification of Step 1. This gives $0\to\mathcal O_{X^b}^{\oplus r}\xrightarrow{\alpha^b}\mathcal F^b\to\mathcal H^b\to0$. For compatibility, a pulled-back module map sends a section supported on the inverse image of the exceptional divisor to a section with the same support condition. Consequently it induces the map on the quotients defining strict transform [def-trf-module-strict-transform]. If $\pi_i$ are the quotient maps, the induced maps satisfy $\alpha^b\pi_1=\pi_2p^*\alpha$ and $h^b\pi_2=\pi_3p^*h$ by their definition on quotient classes; these equalities uniquely determine them since each $\pi_i$ is surjective.

By [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change], $W^b\to S^b$ is surjective. The pullback of the inverse of $\alpha|_W$ is an inverse to $(p^*\alpha)|_{W^b}$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. On this open the two ordinary pullbacks are therefore isomorphic. That isomorphism identifies their subsheaves of exceptional-supported sections [def-trf-module-strict-transform], because both it and its inverse commute with restriction. Their quotients are isomorphic, and Step 2 identifies this quotient isomorphism with $\alpha^b|_{W^b}$. In particular $\mathcal F^b|_{W^b}=\mathcal O_{W^b}^{\oplus r}$ via $\alpha^b$.

source.place: Tag 0815, theorem-flatten-module, paragraph 3, preservation of the generic basis under blowup.

proof.text: Fix an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S^b$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1),(2), its full inverse image $Y=X\times_SV$ is affine, say $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), $Y\to V$ is smooth; [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion] gives flatness and local finite presentation. The ring map $R\to A$ is finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation]. It is flat by [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], applied to the structure sheaf (whose stalk flatness is exactly flatness of the morphism). Its fibres are geometrically integral: for $v\in V$ mapping to $s\in S$, the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $Y_v$ with $X_s\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)$. After any further field extension it is still the corresponding extension of $X_s$, hence integral by hypothesis. These identifications are the unique maps commuting with the projections, so require no hypothesis on the blowup base.

source.place: Tag 0815, theorem-flatten-module, application of Tag 05I3 after blowup; morphisms.tex Tags 01VB, 01VE, 01VF, 01TQ.

proof.text: Put $N=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal F^b)$ and let $\beta:A^{\oplus r}\to N$ correspond to $\alpha^b|_Y$. The counit and unit of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] identify $\mathcal F^b|_Y$ with $\widetilde N$ and the sheaf map with $\widetilde\beta$; its preservation of colimits identifies $\mathcal H^b|_Y$ with $\widetilde Q$ for $Q=\operatorname{coker}\beta$, using Step 2. The module $N$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](a), since Step 1 supplied finite type. The stalks of these sheaves at a prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$ are $N_{\mathfrak q}$ and $Q_{\mathfrak q}$ by [lem-sbc-affine-module-germ-localization]. For each $\mathfrak p\subset R$, the open $W^b\cap Y_{\mathfrak p}$ is nonempty by Step 3. An open containing a point of an integral fibre contains its generic point: in a domain every nonempty basic open contains the zero prime. Therefore its generic point $\xi_{\mathfrak p}$ lies in $W^b$. At that point Step 3 identifies $N_{\xi_{\mathfrak p}}$ with $A_{\xi_{\mathfrak p}}^{\oplus r}$, which is $R_{\mathfrak p}$-flat since $Y\to V$ is flat. It also makes $\beta\otimes_A\kappa(\xi_{\mathfrak p})$ an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0815, theorem-flatten-module, paragraph 3; Tag 05I3, lemma-induction-step, generic-basis hypotheses.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-free-subtraction-flatness] to $R\to A$, $N$, $\beta$ and $Q$. Step 4 verifies flat finite presentation and geometric integrality of every fibre; Step 5 verifies finiteness, generic flatness and the residue-field basis condition for every base prime. For a point $y\in Y$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q\subset A$ and image $t\in V$ corresponding to $\mathfrak p$, it gives $N_{\mathfrak q}$ flat over $R_{\mathfrak p}$ if and only if $Q_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R_{\mathfrak p}$. By the stalk identifications of Step 5 these are exactly $\mathcal F^b_y$, $\mathcal H^b_y$ and $\mathcal O_{S^b,t}$. Every $t\in S^b$ has an affine neighbourhood by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], so this proves the equivalence at every $y$. Taking all stalks gives the equivalence of relative flatness in [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over].
